source.title: Ball-Evans approximation problem: recent progress and open problems

accepted.question_text: Let Ω ⊂ R^n with n ≥ 3, and let f be a homeomorphism in the Sobolev space W^{1,p}(Ω, R^n). The Ball-Evans approximation problem asks whether such a Sobolev homeomorphism can be approximated in the W^{1,p} norm by a sequence of diffeomorphisms or by a sequence of piecewise affine homeomorphisms. Prove or disprove that this approximation is always possible in dimensions n ≥ 3.

evidence.quote: The Ball-Evans approximation problems asks for the approximation of homeomorphism f in the Sobolev space W1,p(Ω, R^n) by a sequence of diffeomorphisms (or piecewise affine homeomorphisms) in the norm of Sobolev space.

Open problem 1. Ball-Evans problem in dimension n ≥ 3: Prove or disprove that W1,p Sobolev homeomorphism in dimension n ≥ 3 can be approximated by a sequence of diffeomorphism (or piecewise affine homeomorphisms).

accepted.question_text: Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open with n ≥ 3, and let f: Ω → R^n be a piecewise affine homeomorphism. Is every such map approximable by diffeomorphisms in the Sobolev norm? In other words, does piecewise affine approximability imply diffeomorphic approximability in dimensions n ≥ 3?
accepted.context_brief: From piecewise affine to diffeomorphic approximation

evidence.quote: Open problem 2. Piecewise affine implies diffeomorphic approximation for n ≥ 3: Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open and n ≥ 3. Show that given piecewise affine homeomorphism f : Ω → R^n we can approximate it by diffeomorphisms in the Sobolev norm.
It seems very reasonable that similar should be true at least for n = 3 but it was not shown yet.

accepted.question_text: For some dimension n in higher dimensions and some exponent p ≥ floor(n/2), does there exist a counterexample to the Ball-Evans approximation problem; that is, a homeomorphism f ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω, R^n) that cannot be approximated in the Sobolev norm by diffeomorphisms or piecewise affine homeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: The Ball-Evans approximation problems asks for the approximation of homeomorphism f in the Sobolev space W1,p(Ω, R^n) by a sequence of diffeomorphisms (or piecewise affine homeomorphisms) in the norm of Sobolev space.
Open problem 3. Possible counterexample for p ≥ [n/2]: Is it possible to construct a counterexample to Ball-Evans approximation problem for some p ≥ [n/2] in higher dimensions?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω ⊂ R^2 be open, let f: Ω → R^2 be a homeomorphism with Jf > 0 almost everywhere, let p ≥ 1, and let a > 0. Define E1(f) = ∫_Ω (|Df(x)|^p + 1/Jf(x)^a) dx and E2(f) = ∫_Ω (|Df(x)|^2 + |Df(x)|^2/Jf(x)) dx. Can one find a sequence of diffeomorphisms that approximates f in the Sobolev norm and also approximates f with respect to the energy functional E1 or E2?

evidence.quote: Open problem 4. Ball-Evans problem for more general functionals: Given an open set Ω ⊂ R^2 and a homeomorphism f : Ω → R^2 with Jf > 0 a.e., p ≥ 1 and a > 0 let us define E1(f) := Z Ω ( |Df(x)|^p + 1/Jf(x)^a ) dx and E2(f) := Z Ω ( |Df(x)|^2 + |Df(x)|^2 / Jf(x) ) dx. Can we find an approximating sequence of diffeomorphisms which approximate f well both in the Sobolev norm and also in the E1 or E2 functional?

accepted.question_text: Let f ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω, R^n) be a homeomorphism whose Jacobian satisfies Jf ≡ 1 almost everywhere, so that f is incompressible. Can f be approximated in the Sobolev norm by a sequence of incompressible diffeomorphisms, or by piecewise affine incompressible homeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Therefore in many modeling situations we actually work with incompressible deformations assuming that Jf ≡ 1 a.e.

Open problem 5. Ball-Evans mapping for incompressible homeomorphisms: Let f ∈ W1,p(Ω, R^n) be a homeomorphism with Jf ≡ 1 a.e. Can we find a sequence of incompressible diffeomorphisms (or piecewise affine incompressible homeomorphisms) which approximate f in the Sobolev norm?

accepted.question_text: Let f ∈ W^{2,q}(Ω, R^n) with q ≥ 1 be a homeomorphism. Is there a sequence of diffeomorphisms, or a sequence of piecewise affine homeomorphisms, that converges to f in the W^{2,q} Sobolev norm?

evidence.quote: where q ∈ [1,∞) and δ0 > 0.

Open problem 6. Ball-Evans approximation problem for W2,q homeomorphisms: Let f ∈ W2,q(Ω, R^n), g ≥ 1, be a homeomorphism. Can we find a sequence of diffeomorphisms (or piecewise affine homeomorphisms) which approximate f in the W2,q Sobolev norm?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω, Ω′ ⊂ R^n be bounded open sets with n ≥ 3. Define Hom(Ω, Ω′)_w to be the class of maps f ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω, Ω′) that arise as weak W^{1,p} limits of homeomorphisms from Ω onto Ω′, and define Hom(Ω, Ω′)_{||·||_{W^{1,p}}} to be the class of strong W^{1,p} limits of such homeomorphisms. Is it true that Hom(Ω, Ω′)_w = Hom(Ω, Ω′)_{||·||_{W^{1,p}}} in dimensions n ≥ 3?
accepted.context_brief: Weak versus strong closure of homeomorphisms

evidence.quote: Hom(Ω, Ω′)_w := { f ∈ W1,p(Ω, Ω′) : there are homeomorphisms fk from Ω onto Ω′ with fk → f weakly in W1,p }.
where Hom(Ω, Ω′)_{||·||W1,p} and Diff (Ω, Ω′)_{||·||W1,p} denote the class of strong limits of homeomorphisms and diffeomorphisms in the W1,p norm.
Open problem 7. Weak and strong closure of homeomorphisms for n ≥ 3: Let n ≥ 3, is it true that Hom(Ω, Ω′)_w = Hom(Ω, Ω′)_{||·||W1,p}?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω, Ω′ ⊂ R^n be bounded open sets with n ≥ 3. Define Diff(Ω, Ω′)_w to be the class of maps f ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω, Ω′) that arise as weak W^{1,p} limits of diffeomorphisms from Ω onto Ω′, and define Diff(Ω, Ω′)_{||·||_{W^{1,p}}} to be the class of strong W^{1,p} limits of such diffeomorphisms. Is it true that Diff(Ω, Ω′)_w = Diff(Ω, Ω′)_{||·||_{W^{1,p}}} in dimensions n ≥ 3?
accepted.context_brief: Weak versus strong closure of diffeomorphisms

evidence.quote: Diff (Ω, Ω′)_w := { f ∈ W1,p(Ω, Ω′) : there are diffeomorphisms fk from Ω onto Ω′ with fk → f weakly in W1,p }.
where Hom(Ω, Ω′)_{||·||W1,p} and Diff (Ω, Ω′)_{||·||W1,p} denote the class of strong limits of homeomorphisms and diffeomorphisms in the W1,p norm.
Open problem 8. Weak and strong closure of diffeomorphisms for n ≥ 3: Let n ≥ 3, is it true that Diff (Ω, Ω′)_w = Diff (Ω, Ω′)_{||·||W1,p}?

accepted.question_text: Let n ≥ 4 and p = floor(n/2). If Ω ⊂ R^n is a connected open set and f ∈ W^{1,floor(n/2)}(Ω, R^n) is a homeomorphism, is it possible that the sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} both have positive measure?
accepted.context_brief: Jacobian sign in the limiting exponent case

evidence.quote: Open problem 9. The limiting case p = [n/2]: Let n ≥ 4 and p = [n/2]. Let Ω ⊂ R^n be connected open set and let f ∈ W1,[n/2](Ω, R^n) be a homeomorphism. Is it possible that both sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} have positive measure?

accepted.question_text: Let n ≥ 4 and 1 ≤ p < floor(n/2). Is it possible to construct a homeomorphism f ∈ W^{1,p}(B(0,R), B(0,R)) such that f(x) = x on the boundary ∂B(0,R) and Jf < 0 almost everywhere in [0,1]^n?

evidence.quote: Open problem 10. Can we have Jf < 0 a.e. for all p < [n/2]: Let n ≥ 4 and 1 ≤ p < [n/2]. Is it possible to construct a homeomorphism f ∈ W1,p(B(0, R), B(0, R)) such that f(x) = x for x ∈ ∂B(0, R) and Jf < 0 a.e. in [0, 1]^n?

accepted.question_text: Let n ≥ 3 and let p satisfy floor(n/2) < p ≤ n−1, or 1 ≤ p ≤ 2 when n = 3. Suppose Ω ⊂ R^n is connected and f ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω, R^n) is continuous, open, and discrete. Is it possible that both sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} have positive measure?
accepted.context_brief: Jacobian sign for continuous open discrete maps

evidence.quote: The usual way how to prove that the mapping f : Ω → R^n in question is in fact a homeomorphism is to first show that it is continuous, open (maps open sets to open sets) and discrete (preimage of single point does not have an accumulation point in Ω).

Open problem 11. Sign of the Jacobian for continuous, open and discrete mappings: Let n ≥ 3 and [n/2] < p ≤ n−1 (or 1 ≤ p ≤ 2 for n = 3). Let Ω ⊂ R^n be connected open set and let f ∈ W1,p(Ω, R^n) be a continuous, open and discrete mapping. Is it possible that both sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} have positive measure?

accepted.question_text: Let n ≥ 6 and 1 ≤ q ≤ floor(n/2)/2. If Ω ⊂ R^n is a connected open set and f ∈ W^{2,q}(Ω, R^n) is a homeomorphism, is it possible that the sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} both have positive measure?
accepted.context_brief: Jacobian sign for second-order Sobolev homeomorphisms

evidence.quote: Open problem 12. Sign of the Jacobian for W2,p mappings: Let n ≥ 6 and 1 ≤ q ≤ [n/2]/2. Let Ω ⊂ R^n be connected open set and let f ∈ W2,q(Ω, R^n) be a homeomorphism. Is it possible that both sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} have positive measure?

accepted.question_text: Let n ≥ 3 and 1 ≤ q < n/2. Is it possible to construct a homeomorphism f in the Sobolev space W^{2,q} with Jacobian Jf = 0 almost everywhere? The same question is also asked for homeomorphisms whose first-order derivative belongs to the space of bounded variation, that is, for f ∈ WBV.
accepted.context_brief: Vanishing Jacobian in W2,q or WBV

evidence.quote: Open problem 13. Can the Jacobian of W2,1 (or W BV ) homeomorphism vanish: Let n ≥ 3 and 1 ≤ q < n/2. Is it possible to construct a Sobolev W2,q homeomorphism with Jf = 0 a.e.? The same problem could be asked also for f ∈ W BV, i.e. for homeomorphism with first order derivative in the space of bounded variation.
